title: Oracle: OD-14 rules BL-15 — caption-split matching stays per-cue
body:
Oracle ruling on the logged evidence `BL-15` (with `BL-8`), dispatched by the unattended delivery driver on base `run/web`.

**OD-14** — `R1002`'s caption-split matching is **per-cue**. A split that straddles two cues stays out of scope, which is the proposed default `BL-15` was filed with.

- No requirement is added and none is superseded: the ruling settles the reading of `R1002` rather than changing it.
- The decision records honestly that **no vision statement decided it** — it is argued against `V1`, which pushes toward recovering every mention, and answers that pressure rather than claiming support it does not have.
- The reasoning: `BL-8`'s and `BL-9`'s measured losses were total per-video blindness, while a cue-boundary split costs at most individual mentions of a signal the design already treats as redundant — a board under discussion is named several times (§6), a title hit auto-includes (`R4`), and a description hit auto-includes (`R1004`). No video's visibility rests on the population this leaves out.
- It also states the limit of its own evidence: all three of `BL-8`'s failures were measured, whereas **no cue-spanning miss has ever been observed** — that population is hypothesized.

This unblocks the OD-6 plan, which stopped at exactly this question. The handoff is at `docs/oracle/handoff-2026-08-20-2.md`.

Opened by the server-side `open-pr` workflow at the driver's request (ESC-50).
